title: HTML & CSS
summary: The structure and style of every web page, with a live preview.

lessons.title: HTML & CSS: syntax basics

concept.text:
HTML describes **what** is on a page using elements written as tags, such as `

` for a heading and `

` for a paragraph. CSS describes **how it looks** using rules: a selector picks elements, and declarations set properties like colour and size.
concept.analogy: HTML is the frame and rooms of a house. CSS is the paint, furniture and lighting. You can redecorate (CSS) without knocking down walls (HTML).

steps.title: Write an element
steps.text: Most elements have an opening tag, content and a closing tag. Attributes add detail inside the opening tag.

steps.title: Nest elements
steps.text: Elements go inside other elements, forming a tree. Indent to show the nesting.

steps.title: Style with a rule
steps.text: Put CSS in a `<style>` block or a separate file. Target a tag name, a `.class` or an `#id`.

lessons.title: HTML & CSS: the box model, flexbox and semantics

concept.text:
Every element is a rectangular box with four layers: content, padding, border and margin. Layout is the art of arranging those boxes. **Flexbox** arranges boxes in a row or column and shares out the space between them.

**Semantic** elements like `<nav>`, `<main>` and `<button>` describe meaning, not appearance. Screen readers and search engines rely on them.
concept.analogy: The box model is a framed picture: the photo is the content, the mat is padding, the frame is the border, and the gap to the next picture on the wall is margin.

visual.caption: The box model, from the outside in.

layers.name: Margin
layers.detail: Transparent space outside the box, pushing neighbours away

layers.name: Border
layers.detail: The visible edge of the box

layers.name: Padding
layers.detail: Space inside the border, around the content

steps.title: Make sizes predictable
steps.text: By default, width excludes padding and border. This one rule makes width mean the whole box.

steps.title: Turn on flexbox
steps.text: Set `display: flex` on the parent. Children line up in a row. `gap` spaces them, `justify-content` spreads them along the row, `align-items` aligns them across it.
steps.code: .row { display: flex; gap: 1rem; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; }

steps.title: Go responsive
steps.text: A media query applies CSS only at certain screen widths.

steps.title: Use the right element
steps.text: A `<button>` is focusable and works with a keyboard for free. A clickable `<div>` is not. Prefer semantic HTML first.

challenge.prompt: Create a navigation bar: a site name on the left and three links on the right, all vertically centred on one row.
challenge.hint: Use `<nav>` as a flex container with `justify-content: space-between` and `align-items: center`. Put the links in their own flex `<div>` with a `gap`.
challenge.solution:
MySite
Home About Contact

takeaways: Every element is a box: content, padding, border, margin.
Flexbox lays out children in one direction and distributes space.
Semantic HTML gives you accessibility and SEO for free.

lessons.title: HTML & CSS mini project: a profile card

concept.text: Time to combine structure, the box model and flexbox into one polished component: a profile card like the ones on team pages. Components like this are the building blocks of real sites.
concept.analogy: You have learned individual chords. A component is your first whole song: the same few chords, arranged with intent.

nodes.label: 1. Structure
nodes.detail: Write the HTML with no styling

steps.title: Structure first
steps.text: An `<article>` holds an avatar, a name, a role and a button. Get the content right before any CSS.

steps.title: Lay it out
steps.text: Centre the card's content with flexbox in a column, and give the card a fixed max-width.

steps.title: Style and polish
steps.text: Add a border radius, a soft shadow and a hover state on the button. Use `transition` so the change feels smooth.

challenge.hint: Add a `<div class="stats">` with three children and make it a flex row with `gap` or `justify-content: space-around` and `width: 100%`.

takeaways: Build components in order: structure, layout, style, polish.
Flexbox in a column with align-items: center is the quickest way to centre a stack.
Small details such as radius, shadow and hover states make a design feel finished.
